sources.entry: Netron - Visualizer for neural network and machine learning models. (Source Code) MIT Python/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Netron is a viewer for visually inspecting neural network, deep learning and machine learning model files in a browser or as a desktop or Python app.
summary.what_it_does: Netron opens trained model files and displays their computation graphs so you can inspect layers, connections and structure. The README says it supports ONNX, TensorFlow Lite, PyTorch, torch.export, ExecuTorch, TorchScript, TensorFlow, Core ML, OpenVINO, Keras, Caffe, Darknet, Safetensors and NumPy. It lists experimental support for MLIR, JAX, GGUF, RKNN, ncnn, MNN, PaddlePaddle and scikit-learn. It can be used through a browser version, native installers for macOS, Linux and Windows, or a Python package that starts a local viewer for a given file. The README includes links to sample models for several formats to try it out.
use_cases: view ONNX or TensorFlow Lite model graphs
check layers of a PyTorch or Keras model
explore a GGUF or Safetensors model file
open a Core ML model on macOS
how_to_run: Browser: open the browser version via the Start link in the README
macOS: brew install --cask netron (or download the .dmg)
Windows: winget install -s winget netron (or download the .exe installer)
notable: Supports a wide range of model formats from many frameworks in one viewer
Runs in the browser with no install required
Available as a desktop app for macOS, Linux and Windows
Python package can launch the viewer for a file from code
caveats: Support for MLIR, JAX, GGUF, RKNN, ncnn, MNN, PaddlePaddle and scikit-learn is experimental
The README does not state platform limits or file size limits
keywords: see layers of my neural network
